deviations.what: An unplanned fix was added ahead of the remaining waves: the literal OpenShell credential placeholder marker was reworded out of five tracked files, and scripts/scan-secrets.py now fails on it. Tasks t2 and t3 moved from agents runs to Claude subagents on the host.
deviations.reason: Three agents runs of t2 on the OpenCode harness failed: two because the harness read the marker and the egress proxy refused its next model request, one because of the 1 MiB write chunk. The owner chose 'Fix it first' on 2026-11-26.

deviations.what: Observability was added to the D2 design mid-run: a new decision (c66), four proposed claims (c67 to c70), one assumption (c71) and one proposed plan task for run tracing to a local Langfuse.
deviations.reason: The owner asked for it on 2026-11-26 after three OpenCode runs shared one local model with no way to see the load: 'We should have observability and it should be part of the design. We can run langfuse locally.'

deviations.what: Task t13 built operator questions end to end for the stub driver only. The Claude Code and OpenCode drivers got no ask path and still report the answer capability as unsupported, although the t1 probe found both harnesses can ask.
deviations.reason: The task instruction says to build exactly what the probe record says each harness supports. The agent had no sandbox or credentials to run either real harness, and the contract allows a capability to be reported supported only once measured as this core drives it, so it left both unsupported and said so in its report. All four acceptance criteria of t13 are met as written; the spec's claim that an operator can answer a real harness's question is not delivered.

evidence.test_ref: core/test/runs/restart.test.ts::a worker survives a daemon SIGKILL: reported from disk, control reattached, counted against a limit, terminal state reached
evidence.behavior_text: After a SIGKILL of the core and a new core, the surviving worker's run is controllable again and reaches its terminal state
evidence.contract_text: After a restart the core reattaches to every worker whose control socket answers, and a steer, cancel or attach sent to that run takes effect; a worker whose socket does not answer is reported 'unknown' and is never signalled or killed. This supersedes the D1 obligation that live control is unavailable after a restart.
evidence.strength_basis: real daemon and real worker processes; ran green at the named commit. A second test covers a worker that misses its first ping (reattach-retry.test.ts)

evidence.test_ref: core/test/runs/concurrent.test.ts::a per-repository limit refuses the submit past it with limit_reached naming the limit; nothing is queued
evidence.behavior_text: With runsPerRepository 2 the third submit is refused limit_reached naming the limit and its value, and no run directory is created; with no limit 3 submits are accepted
evidence.contract_text: A submit to a repository with active runs is accepted while the stated bound has room and refused with a typed error naming the bound when it has not; the bound is readable through the API, and no submit is queued silently.
evidence.strength_basis: real daemon; ran green at the named commit

evidence.test_ref: core/test/runs/isolation.test.ts::2 runs in 1 repository complete; each runs branch holds only its own commits; the host checkout and index are unchanged; no worktree
evidence.behavior_text: Two concurrent stub runs each return only their own commits on runs/<id>; checkout, index, HEAD and config are byte-identical; no git worktree exists
evidence.contract_text: A run never writes the host checkout, index or any ref outside its own `runs/<id>` branch, and no code path creates a git worktree; two concurrent runs in one repository leave each branch holding only its own run's commits.
evidence.strength_basis: real git and the stub harness, not an OpenShell sandbox; ran green at the named commit. This test failed once before the merge (review finding 19); the cause was fixed and it passed 200 of 200 under load after

evidence.test_ref: core/test/runs/idempotency.test.ts::a repeated submit key returns the first run and creates nothing; a changed request is conflict; both hold after a restart
evidence.behavior_text: The key file and request digest are on disk; a repeat returns the first run with replayed true; a changed request is conflict; both hold after SIGKILL and restart
evidence.contract_text: The key and a digest of the request are on disk before the submit is acknowledged; a repeat of the same key and request returns the first run's id and creates nothing; the same key with a different request returns 'conflict'; both hold after a core restart. Steer and cancel behave the same on their keys.
evidence.strength_basis: real daemon; ran green at the named commit

evidence.test_ref: core/test/runs/questions.test.ts::a question survives a core restart and its answer is delivered into the same run exactly once
evidence.behavior_text: A question is in the log before the wait, is pending after a SIGKILL restart, takes one answer, and a second answer is conflict
evidence.contract_text: A question is appended to the run's on-disk log before the run starts waiting, is listed as pending after a core restart, and an answer is delivered exactly once into the same run; a harness that cannot ask reports the capability as unsupported and 'answer' is refused with the typed error.
evidence.strength_basis: real daemon and worker with the STUB harness only; Claude Code and OpenCode report answer as unsupported (deviation d3), so no real harness was asked

evidence.test_ref: core/test/runs/branches.test.ts::removal deletes only a finished, reachable branch with git branch -d, and reports every skip
evidence.behavior_text: Only a finished run's branch whose tip another non-run ref contains is deleted, with git branch -d and never -D; active, unknown, unreadable and unmerged branches are skipped and reported
evidence.contract_text: Listing shows every `runs/<id>` branch with its run's state; removal deletes a branch only when git itself shows its commits reachable from another ref, never forces a delete, and skips and reports a branch whose run is active, 'unknown' or retained.
evidence.strength_basis: real git; ran green at the named commit. A further test refuses a remote-tracking copy of a run branch as evidence

evidence.test_ref: core/test/daemon/lifecycle.test.ts::SIGTERM sent at the moment of the listening report stops the daemon cleanly (handlers are installed first)
evidence.behavior_text: A SIGTERM arriving at the listening line stops the daemon with exit 0 and removes the socket; a cancel whose grace ends during retention cleanup leaves retained.json (worker/recovery-gaps.test.ts)
evidence.contract_text: The daemon's signal handlers are installed before it reports that it is listening, and a cancel whose grace period ends during retention cleanup still leaves a retention record.
evidence.strength_basis: real daemon child; ran green at the named commit. One line of the third D1 gap (a conflict reply) cannot be reached and is not tested

evidence.test_ref: core/test/publish/broker.test.ts::with the broker down nothing is lost: after it returns every missed event is published once, in order, with its original id
evidence.behavior_text: With the broker down a run reaches the same terminal state and log; when it returns every event is published once, in order, with its original id and append time
evidence.contract_text: An event is published only after it is appended to the run's log, in the broker's existing envelope with the run id; with the broker stopped, a run reaches the same terminal state and the same log, and no call to the core blocks or fails because of the broker.
evidence.strength_basis: in-process MQTT broker on loopback; ran green at the named commit. Not run against the events-cli broker of a real host

evidence.test_ref: core/test/runs/submitter.test.ts::a run submitted over the socket records the user that owns the socket, and no request field changes it
evidence.behavior_text: The stored submitter is the socket owner's uid; a forged submitter in the request body is refused or ignored
evidence.contract_text: The submitter stored on a run is the socket peer the core observed, appears in the run's contract shape, and cannot be set or changed by any request field.
evidence.strength_basis: real daemon; ran green at the named commit. Node cannot read peer credentials, so the submitter is the socket's owner, not the connecting process
